text:
Leah: quick check-in on the Parallel Surface split idea. goal: extract request-router + tenant-shim into a lightweight service so we can iterate on routing policies without touching hot inference paths. want to avoid DB schema migrations during initial phase.

Diego: +1. main risk is dual-writes / stale reads if we run both surfaces in parallel. how do we keep state consistent for session affinity?

Sam: proposal: keep a single canonical session store (redis) for now, but add a routing-layer token that denotes authoritative surface. new surface writes to redis and tags keys with `surface:v2`. reader logic: prefer `surface:v2` if present, else fallback to `surface:v1`. will require small read path change but no DB migration.

Priya: that's reasonable but we need an idempotency and reconciliation plan. if v2 write fails, you can get half-updates. suggest async reconciliation job that scans mismatched keys and repairs based on latest timestamp. also add a `last-modified` ms field.

Leah: agree on reconciliation. can we express that as a recoverability SLA? eg: eventual-consistency window < 10m for session props. if reconciliation backlog > 10k keys then auto-throttle v2 traffic.

Diego: ops ask: what about telemetry and cost attribution while both surfaces run? want per-surface metrics and per-tenant breakdown. add headers `x-surface` + `x-tenant` and ensure tracing spans include surface.

Sam: implemented a small shim that injects `x-surface` today. will push dashboard panels. ETA 3d.

Priya: product: feature flags per-tenant are required. we must be able to flip any tenant back to v1 instantly if we see regressions on quality or latency. Also need a canary group selection that excludes customers on reserved capacity.

Leah: rollout plan draft:
- stage 0 (dev): local + staging smoke 
- stage 1 (canary): 10 internal tenants + 3 low-risk external tenants for 2w
- stage 2 (cohort): 20% of traffic by tenant cohort for 1w 
- stage 3 (ramp): gradual 50% -> 100% over 2w with monitoring gates
Gates: P95 latency <= baseline*1.25, error-rate delta < 0.3%, correctness eval pass-rate >= 99%.

Diego: add circuit-breaker: if P95 > baseline*1.5 or error-rate > 1% -> immediate rollback for affected tenants. Also add quota for reconciliation job so it can't saturate redis.

infra-bot: applied feature-flagging rule `surface.v2.canary` for tenants [int-*] (change-id: ff-2025-09-03-04) :white_check_mark:

Sam: implementation notes:
- keep compatibility layer: API surface v1 continues to proxy to v2 handlers when flag enabled.
- library change: small client shim `routing.v2` to read `x-surface` and prefer v2 keys.
- plan to deprecate v1 adapter after 12 weeks of stable traffic. open debt ticket RED-2025 for adapter removal.

Priya: legal/security: confirm no new PI stored in session keys. If we add any PII we must use tokenized IDs and add KMS audit.

Leah: action items:
- @Sam: push dashboard + client shim (ETA 3d)
- @Diego: reconciliation job spec + redis safety quota (ETA 1w)
- @Priya: canary tenant list + reserved-capacity exclude (ETA EOD)
- @Leah: write cutover runbook + rollback playbook (ETA 2d)

Priya: will share tenant list by EOD. also requesting a short retro after stage1 to capture debt we create.

Leah: thanks all. i'll author a minimal RFC with sequence diagrams and the rollback checklist. scheduling a 30m sync tomorrow to walk implementers.

Diego: one more thought 1. when we deprecate v1, create a telemetry-only window where v1 writes are disabled but reads still succeed to validate no unseen deps. 2. mark all deprecated adapters in codebase with TODO+owner for tracing.

Sam: noted. will include telemetry-only toggle in runbook.

infra-bot: scheduled sync meeting (change-id: meet-2025-09-03-15) :calendar:
